words.ex: When the famous poet died, every national paper printed a long obituary describing her life and work.
In today's editorial, the paper argues that the city needs more cycle lanes and fewer car parks.
The editor herself wrote this morning's leader, calling on the council to save the old cinema.
Three reporters were sent to Muynak to cover the music festival held every year beside the old rusting fishing boats.
Our neighbour found a second-hand piano for half the shop price in the classified ads, squeezed between an offer of a used car and a lost-cat notice.
On Saturdays the newspaper is twice as thick because of the weekend supplement on travel and food.
This month's magazine has a twelve-page feature on young engineers building robots in Andijan.
Teenagers write to the agony column when they don't know how to deal with a bossy friend or exam stress.
The magazine's agony aunt receives hundreds of letters a week from readers who feel lonely or stressed.
Since it started printing puzzles and comics for kids, the magazine's circulation has doubled.
Madina's journal from her exchange year in Japan, full of sketches and train tickets, is now her favourite souvenir.
Every Friday, parents at our school receive an email newsletter with news about exams, clubs and trips.
The student society printed a short pamphlet setting out its political case for lowering the voting age to sixteen.
The football club issued a press release confirming that its new coach would start in July.
While we were waiting, the nurse gave me a leaflet with simple tips on healthy eating.
The travel agency gave us a glossy brochure full of photos of guesthouses in the Nurata hills.
Our school's careers room has a whole shelf of college prospectuses, so you can compare fees and courses before you apply.
Volunteers stood outside the sports centre handing out flyers for Saturday's charity fun run.
Every candidate receives a thin twelve-page booklet explaining the exam rules, from which pens are allowed to what to do if you feel ill.
